blog_title: DTF Order Form Pieces vs Sheets Explained — Why 1 Piece Means a Full Print Sheet, Not 1 T-Shirt
caption: ❌ Common DTF mistake: 'Pieces' ≠ T-shirts. On Sale91's DTF form, 'Pieces' means how many times your *entire uploaded sheet* prints—not individual shirts. Price = sheet height × pieces. Upload ONE gang sheet with all your designs stacked/arranged together, not separate sheets per design. One sheet at 22.8" wide can hold dozens of prints. Stack them smart, print once, cut costs. 📊 Have you been uploading one design per sheet?

editorial_review.reason: All substantive claims are supported by supplied sources: 'Pieces' means whole-sheet reprints (dtf_pieces_whole_sheet), price formula is sheet height × pieces (dtf_pieces_whole_sheet), sheet width is 22.8 inches (dtf_sheet_size), and one sheet can carry many designs as a gang sheet (dtf_sheet_size). The caption correctly teaches the core buyer lesson—uploading separate sheets per design multiplies orders and costs—without inventing prices, guarantees, or unverified claims. The question at the end engages without overstating.
